Qin

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Influences of Combined Traffic Noise on the Ability of Learning and Memory in Mice

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Mice exposed for six weeks to recorded combined highway and high-speed-railway noise, assessed by water-maze learning and hippocampal neurotransmitters.
span.quote: The present study aimed to evaluate the influences of combined traffic noise (CTN) on the ability of learning and memory in mice.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Furthermore, those effects were regulated and controlled by the level of glutamate in the hippocampus.

span.label: traffic-noise effects on spatial learning and memory
span.quote: The present study aimed to evaluate the influences of combined traffic noise (CTN) on the ability of learning and memory in mice.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: On the basis of behavioral reactions in Morris water maze (MWM) and the concentrations of amino acid neurotransmitters in the hippocampus, the impacts of CTN on learning and memory in mice were examined.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A low-dose stressor breaks homeostasis and triggers a compensatory response that overshoots the inhibition, producing facilitation early on.
span.quote: Under the condition of low-dose stimulation, the compensatory response produced by organisms could be greater than the inhibitory response of stimuli, which resulted in the excitatory effect of stimuli.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: With continued exposure the compensatory response is exhausted, so the inhibitory effect of the noise comes to dominate.
span.quote: It could be caused by a gradual exhaustion of compensatory response.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Glutamate acting on hippocampal NMDA receptors admits calcium and thereby changes synaptic plasticity, which is the substrate of learning and memory.
span.quote: Subsequently, Mg 2+ , which blocked the channel of Ca 2+ , was removed, and the Ca 2+ flowed into the cell, which induced the change of synaptic plasticity.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The behavioural swing is mediated by the hippocampal glutamate level, which is raised by short exposure and lowered by long exposure.
span.quote: Thus, it could be speculated that the effects of CTN on the ability of learning and memory in mice were regulated and controlled by the level of Glu in the hippocampus.

span.label: The direction of the effect reverses with exposure duration, which the paper identifies as hormesis - excitation at low dose, inhibition at high
span.quote: Hormesis was the common biphasic dose-effect model in toxicology and was characterized by low-dose excitement and high-dose inhibition.[ 22 ]

span.label: Dose for noise is not the level but the level multiplied by the duration, which is why the same decibel figure sits on both sides of the curve
span.quote: Corresponding to the dose of toxicity that was ingested by organisms, the exposure dose of noise for organisms was the value of exposure sound level times exposure duration.[ 25 ]

span.label: The reversal is attributed to a compensatory response that outruns the insult at first and is then exhausted
span.quote: Under the condition of low-dose stimulation, the compensatory response produced by organisms could be greater than the inhibitory response of stimuli, which resulted in the excitatory effect of stimuli.

span.label: The behavioural reversal is tracked by glutamate, which rises early and falls late while GABA stays flat
span.quote: Obviously, the level of Glu in mice rose after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decrease in the Glu level in mice.

span.label: Glutamate has its own inverted-U: more release aids learning until excitotoxicity sets in
span.quote: Nonetheless, too much release of Glu could cause an excitatory toxic effect on the neurons, which resulted in a decline in the learning and memory ability.

span.label: Combined road and rail noise is not the sum of its parts - the two sources differ in continuity, peak level and low-frequency content
span.quote: Highway traffic noise is relatively continuous. However, high-speed railway produces intermittent noise, which is characterized by shorter duration, higher-peak sound level, and more low-frequency components.[ 1 2 ]

span.label: The extrapolation from mice to human cognitive ability is explicitly only a speculation awaiting human testing.
span.quote: Of course, this speculation needs to be verified by additional cognitive behavior tests in humans exposed to 70 dB(A) CTN.

span.label: The compensatory-response account of the biphasic effect is inferred rather than measured.
span.quote: It was speculated that the compensatory response was greater than the inhibitory response of CTN in mice.

span.label: Ten mice per group per batch, with the key contrasts significant in only some batches
span.quote: Each batch ( n = 20) consisted of two groups, that is, the experimental group ( n = 10) and the control group ( n = 10).

span.label: Batches are separate groups of animals rather than repeated measures, so the time course is between-subjects
span.quote: A total of 80 healthy male ICR mice (28 days old, weighing 14.4 ± 1.1 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Centre of Zhejiang Province (Hangzhou, China), and were randomly divided into four batches.

span.label: All animals were male, so nothing here speaks to sex differences
span.quote: A total of 80 healthy male ICR mice (28 days old, weighing 14.4 ± 1.1 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Centre of Zhejiang Province (Hangzhou, China), and were randomly divided into four batches.

span.label: Only one sound level was tested, so the dose-response curve is traced through duration alone
span.quote: The effects of 70 dB(A) CTN on the ability of learning and memory were closely related to the exposure duration.

span.label: The mechanism is inferred from a speculation about compensation rather than measured
span.quote: It was speculated that the compensatory response was greater than the inhibitory response of CTN in mice.

span.label: The human literature the study is motivated by is itself inconsistent, and the paper attributes that to uncontrolled personal and social factors
span.quote: In addition to acoustic factors, the results of epidemiological survey were also influenced by the personal factors of participants (e.g., age, educational level, and physical condition) and social factors (e.g., the level of economic development), which led to an inconsistency in the findings regarding the effects of traffic noise on cognitive ability.

span.label: the hormesis biphasic dose-response model, with noise dose defined by analogy to an ingested toxicant dose (sound level times duration)
span.quote: Corresponding to the dose of toxicity that was ingested by organisms, the exposure dose of noise for organisms was the value of exposure sound level times exposure duration.

span.label: a control group of ten mice per batch held at a background level of no more than 35 dB(A), against 70 +/- 1.5 dB(A) for the exposed group, and never given the combined traffic noise
span.quote: The L Aeq of the background noise was not more than 35 dB(A), which was the intensity presented to the control group.

span.label: short-term exposure
span.quote: Obviously, the ability of learning in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decline in the learning ability of mice

span.label: long-term exposure
span.quote: Obviously, the ability of learning in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decline in the learning ability of mice

span.label: ability of learning
span.quote: Obviously, the ability of learning in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decline in the learning ability of mice

span.label: Mg 2+ → synaptic plasticity
span.note: THE MECHANISM THE SPAN ACTUALLY DESCRIBES, between terms it actually names: magnesium blocked the calcium channel, was removed, and the resulting calcium influx induced the change of synaptic plasticity. A three-step chain, and no edge type carries a chain - each link would have to be asserted separately, losing the ordering that is the content.
span.quote: Subsequently, Mg 2+ , which blocked the channel of Ca 2+ , was removed, and the Ca 2+ flowed into the cell, which induced the change of synaptic plasticity.[ 21 ]

span.label: the effect of 70 dB(A) noise - after SHORT exposure (6-10 days): learning and memory IMPROVE
span.quote: The MWM test showed that the ability of learning and memory in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days, the first batch) to 70 dB(A) CTN, which showed the excitatory effect of stimuli.

span.label: the effect of 70 dB(A) noise - after LONG exposure (26-40 days): learning and memory DECLINE, at the same sound level
span.quote: Long-term exposure (26–30 days, the third batch; 36–40 days, the fourth batch) led to the decline of learning and memory ability, which indicated the inhibitory effect of stimuli.

span.label: dose - as sound level: the 70 dB(A) figure, which is what gets reported and compared across studies
span.quote: whose day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L dn ) was 70 dB(A)

span.label: dose - as level times duration: the quantity that actually determines the sign of the effect
span.quote: Corresponding to the dose of toxicity that was ingested by organisms, the exposure dose of noise for organisms was the value of exposure sound level times exposure duration.[ 25 ]

span.label: glutamate - below the toxic threshold: more release, better learning
span.quote: The individual ability of learning and memory was upregulated by Glu level in the hippocampus, that is, increasing the release of Glu in the hippocampus enhanced the individual ability of learning and memory.

span.label: glutamate - above it: excitotoxic, and learning declines with the same transmitter that improved it
span.quote: Nonetheless, too much release of Glu could cause an excitatory toxic effect on the neurons, which resulted in a decline in the learning and memory ability.

span.label: builds-on → hormesis, the biphasic low-dose-excitation / high-dose-inhibition dose-effect model in toxicology (refs 22-26)
span.quote: This biphasic dose-effect conformed to the characteristics of hormesis.

span.label: replicates → the epidemiological surveys of Haines (ref 8) and Kempen (ref 9) showing declining cognitive ability in children after long-term aircraft or road traffic noise
span.quote: This inhibitory effect of stimuli under long-term noise exposure in humans was similar with that in mice in the present study.

span.label: extends → Calabrese's overcompensation account of hormesis
span.quote: Calabreseci[ 26 ] found that hormesis was caused by an overcompensation mechanism and was a kind of adaptive response by organisms.

span.label: critiques → previous animal noise studies that used white noise, narrow band noise or pure tones instead of real environmental noise
span.quote: However, previous studies adopting the aforementioned method commonly used nonenvironmental noise as the stimulus (such as white noise, narrow band noise, or pure tone), which is different from the actual-environmental noise.[ 14 15 16 ]

span.label: supports → Di et al. on combined road-rail noise being more annoying than a single dominant source at the same level
span.quote: In addition, they found that when the day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L dn ) was greater than 63.5 dB, the percentage of highly annoyed individuals due to the road–rail CTN (the difference in L dn between the two sources was less than or equal to 5 dB) was significantly higher than that due to the one dominant noise (the difference in L dn between the two sources was larger than 5 dB, and the larger one was the dominant noise) with the same L dn .

span.label: combined traffic noise —operationalised-as→ hormesis
span.quote: This biphasic dose-effect conformed to the characteristics of hormesis.

span.label: overcompensation —causes→ hormesis
span.quote: Calabreseci[ 26 ] found that hormesis was caused by an overcompensation mechanism and was a kind of adaptive response by organisms.

span.label: Glu —causes→ synaptic plasticity
span.quote: It was released from the presynaptic membrane, through the synaptic cleft, and would combine with the N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor in the postsynaptic membrane.

span.label: RETRACTED (NEITHER ENDPOINT APPEARS IN THE SPAN, IN ANY FORM) · Glu —part-of→ NMDA
span.note: RETRACTED: NEITHER ENDPOINT APPEARS IN THE SPAN, IN ANY FORM. The edge is `Glu --part-of--> NMDA`. The span reads: 'Subsequently, Mg 2+ , which blocked the channel of Ca 2+ , was removed, and the Ca 2+ flowed into the cell, which induced the change of synaptic plasticity.' It names magnesium, calcium and synaptic plasticity, and neither glutamate nor the NMDA receptor - not as an abbreviation, not as a morphological variant, not at all. Checked against the three explanations that accounted for most of the unattested population (Q-340): derivational morphology, the paper's own acronyms, and irregular plurals. None applies. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): a real mechanism between different terms, housed below. Q-267 would reject this edge today; it predates the rule, which is the stratum Q-340 was written to sweep. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Subsequently, Mg 2+ , which blocked the channel of Ca 2+ , was removed, and the Ca 2+ flowed into the cell, which induced the change of synaptic plasticity.[ 21 ]

span.label: GABA —distinct-from→ Glu
span.quote: GABA is an important inhibitory amino acid neurotransmitter in the CNS. It is converted from Glu via decarboxylation by glutamic acid decarboxylase.[ 28 ]

span.label: GABA —causes→ NMDA
span.quote: GABA could strengthen the blocking effect of Mg 2+ on the NMDA receptor and make difficulties in changing synaptic plasticity mediated by the NMDA receptor.[ 29 ]

span.label: synaptic plasticity —part-of→ hippocampus
span.quote: The change of synaptic plasticity was the basis for individual ability in learning and memory.

span.label: excitatory toxic effect —causes→ Glu
span.quote: Nonetheless, too much release of Glu could cause an excitatory toxic effect on the neurons, which resulted in a decline in the learning and memory ability.

span.label: Morris water maze —operationalised-as→ latencies
span.quote: The relationships between the latencies and the training days of the mice from the experimental and control groups in different batches are shown in Figure 1 .

span.label: target quadrant —part-of→ Morris water maze
span.quote: The percentages of time spent in a target quadrant for the mice from the experimental and control groups in different batches are shown in Figure 3 .

span.label: combined traffic noise —operationalised-as→ day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level
span.term: day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level
span.quote: The Institute of Cancer Research (ICR) mice were exposed to CTN from highways and high-speed railways for 42 days, whose day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L dn ) was 70 dB(A).

span.label: RETRACTED (NEITHER ENDPOINT APPEARS IN THE SPAN) · epidemiological survey —contrasted-with→ ICR
span.note: RETRACTED: NEITHER ENDPOINT APPEARS IN THE SPAN. The edge is `epidemiological survey --contrasted-with--> ICR`. The span is a single sentence about methodology: 'The method employing animal exposure to noise in a controllable laboratory is a good way to make up this shortage.' It names neither epidemiological surveys nor the ICR mouse strain. The contrast the edge records may well be one the paper draws - laboratory animal work against epidemiological survey - but IT IS NOT DRAWN HERE, and 'this shortage' is an anaphor pointing at a sentence the span does not include. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): that controlled animal exposure compensates for a shortcoming named elsewhere. That is a methodological endorsement with its referent outside the span, so nothing is kept for these endpoints. — strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: The method employing animal exposure to noise in a controllable laboratory is a good way to make up this shortage.

span.label: hormesis —causes→ learning rate
span.quote: Obviously, the ability of learning in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decline in the learning ability of mice.

span.label: short-term exposure —causes→ ability of learning
span.note: holds when: 6-10 days of exposure to 70 dB(A) combined traffic noise · direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 1 — ONE OF A PAIR: the SAME exposure carries the OPPOSITE sign at longer durations. Neither edge is the paper's finding alone - the finding is that the sign flips.
span.quote: Obviously, the ability of learning in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decline in the learning ability of mice

span.label: long-term exposure —causes→ ability of learning
span.note: holds when: 26-30 and 36-40 days of exposure · direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 1 — ONE OF A PAIR: see the short-term edge, which carries the opposite sign on the same measure.
span.quote: Obviously, the ability of learning in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decline in the learning ability of mice

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Differences in latency between the experimental and control groups were examined by analysis of variance with repeated measures.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Differences in the percentage of time spent in a target quadrant, learning rate, and the levels of the hippocampal amino acid neurotransmitters between the experimental and control groups were examined by an independent samples t -test.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: All data from the MWM test and assays testing the hippocampal amino acid neurotransmitters were expressed as mean ± SEM (Standard Error of Mean) and analyzed by the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 20.0 software

span.label: p-value
span.quote: Significance was accepted at the level of P < 0.05.

span.label: linear regression
span.quote: On the basis of this, a linear fitting between latencies and training days for each mouse was done, and the absolute value of the linear fitting slope was used to represent its learning rate.

span.label: Six to ten days of exposure to 70 dB(A) combined traffic noise improved learning and memory in mice.
span.quote: The MWM test showed that the ability of learning and memory in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days, the first batch) to 70 dB(A) CTN, which showed the excitatory effect of stimuli.

span.label: Longer exposure reversed the effect, degrading learning and memory.
span.quote: Long-term exposure (26–30 days, the third batch; 36–40 days, the fourth batch) led to the decline of learning and memory ability, which indicated the inhibitory effect of stimuli.

span.label: Learning rate, measured as the slope of latency against training day, was significantly faster in exposed mice only in the first batch.
span.quote: The learning rate of the mice from the experimental group was significantly higher than that for the mice from the control group in the first batch (6–10 days) ( P < 0.05).

span.label: Memory, measured as time in the target quadrant, was significantly better in exposed mice only in the first batch.
span.quote: The percentage of time spent in a target quadrant for the mice from the experimental group was significantly higher than that of the mice from the control group in the first batch (6–10 days) ( P < 0.05).

span.label: Hippocampal glutamate rose with short exposure and fell with long exposure, mirroring the behavioural pattern.
span.quote: Obviously, the level of Glu in mice rose after short-term exposure (6–10 days) to 70 dB(A) CTN, but the long-term exposure (26–30 days, 36–40 days) led to a decrease in the Glu level in mice.

span.label: Hippocampal GABA was unchanged by noise exposure at every time point.
span.quote: The GABA levels of the mice from the experimental group were approximate to those of the mice from the control group in all batches.

span.label: Measured glutamate stayed inside the normal range, ruling out excitotoxicity as the cause of the later decline.
span.quote: On the basis of this, it could be ruled out that too much release of Glu led to an excitatory toxic effect on the neurons in the hippocampus.

span.label: The biphasic time course of the noise effect matches the hormesis dose-response pattern.
span.quote: This biphasic dose-effect conformed to the characteristics of hormesis.

span.label: short exposure to 70 dB(A) combined traffic noise improved water-maze learning and memory
span.quote: The MWM test showed that the ability of learning and memory in mice was improved after short-term exposure (6–10 days, the first batch) to 70 dB(A) CTN, which showed the excitatory effect of stimuli.

span.label: long exposure at the same level degraded them
span.quote: Long-term exposure (26–30 days, the third batch; 36–40 days, the fourth batch) led to the decline of learning and memory ability, which indicated the inhibitory effect of stimuli.

span.label: the intermediate batch showed no difference from control, so the curve passes through zero
span.quote: The learning rate of the mice from the experimental group was approximate to that for the mice from the control group in the second batch (16–20 days).

span.label: hippocampal glutamate rose early and fell late, tracking the behavioural reversal
span.quote: Specifically, the Glu level of the mice from the experimental group was higher than that of the mice from the control group in the first batch (6–10 days).

span.label: GABA did not differ between groups in any batch
span.quote: The GABA levels of the mice from the experimental group were approximate to those of the mice from the control group in all batches.

span.label: the human literature already disagrees about noise and cognition, including one study where 71 dB(A) road noise IMPROVED children's episodic memory
span.quote: However, Stansfeld et al .[ 10 ] found that the road traffic noise whose highest equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L Aeq ) was 71 dB(A) could improve the ability of episodic memory in children.

span.label: hormesis
span.quote: Hormesis was the common biphasic dose-effect model in toxicology and was characterized by low-dose excitement and high-dose inhibition.

span.label: noise exposure dose
span.quote: Corresponding to the dose of toxicity that was ingested by organisms, the exposure dose of noise for organisms was the value of exposure sound level times exposure duration.

span.label: learning rate (operational definition)
span.quote: Therefore, the learning rate could be represented by the absolute value of linear fitting slope between latencies and training days (that was the declining quantity of latency in unit time).

span.label: hidden platform test
span.quote: The hidden platform test was used to assess the learning ability of animals, in which latency was the common indicator.

span.label: probe trail test
span.quote: The probe trail test was used to assess the memory ability of animals, in which the common indicator was the percentage of time spent in a target quadrant.

span.label: combined traffic noise (CTN)
span.quote: To save land resources, the highway and high-speed railway are always constructed in parallel, which results in an increasing number of population being influenced by combined traffic noise (CTN).

span.label: hormesis
span.quote: Hormesis was the common biphasic dose-effect model in toxicology and was characterized by low-dose excitement and high-dose inhibition.[ 22 ]

span.label: exposure dose of noise
span.quote: the exposure dose of noise for organisms was the value of exposure sound level times exposure duration.[ 25 ]

span.label: GABA
span.quote: GABA is an important inhibitory amino acid neurotransmitter in the CNS.

span.label: Glu
span.quote: Glu is one of the excitatory amino acid neurotransmitters in CNS.

span.label: exposure to 70 dB(A) combined traffic noise versus quiet background
span.term: exposure to 70 dB(A) combined traffic noise versus quiet background
span.quote: After an adaptation for 7 days in the laboratory, the mice of the experimental group were continuously exposed to the CTN for 42 days, while for the control group, this was not done.

span.label: exposure duration (batch tested at 6-10, 16-20, 26-30 or 36-40 days)
span.term: exposure duration (batch tested at 6-10, 16-20, 26-30 or 36-40 days)
span.quote: In the present study, the MMW test was performed in mice from four different batches at four different time points during the period of noise exposure, that is, 6–10 days (the first batch), 16–20 days (the second batch), 26–30 days (the third batch), and 36–40 days (the fourth batch).

span.label: escape latency in the hidden platform test
span.term: escape latency in the hidden platform test
span.quote: The hidden platform test was used to assess the learning ability of animals, in which latency was the common indicator.

span.label: percentage of time spent in the target quadrant
span.term: percentage of time spent in the target quadrant
span.quote: The probe trail test was used to assess the memory ability of animals, in which the common indicator was the percentage of time spent in a target quadrant.

span.label: hippocampal glutamate and GABA concentrations
span.quote: A volume of 150 μL was extracted from the supernatants for measuring the levels of Glu and GABA by OPA (O-phthalaldehyd) precolumn derivatization high-performance liquid chromatography.

span.label: housing temperature, humidity and light/dark cycle
span.term: housing temperature, humidity and light/dark cycle
span.quote: Five mice were housed in one cage and were kept in a room with constant temperature (22 ± 2°C), humidity (50–60%), and a 12 h/12 h light/dark cycle (lights on at 08:00, lights off at 20:00).

span.label: timing of the neurotransmitter assay relative to the maze test
span.term: timing of the neurotransmitter assay relative to the maze test
span.quote: To diminish the influences of the MWM test on the levels of neurotransmitters in mice, the levels of amino acid neurotransmitters in the hippocampus were measured after the MWM test for 2 days in each batch of mice.

span.label: exposure duration (batch: 6-10, 16-20, 26-30, 36-40 days)
span.quote: A total of 80 healthy male ICR mice (28 days old, weighing 14.4 ± 1.1 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Centre of Zhejiang Province (Hangzhou, China), and were randomly divided into four batches.

span.label: noise exposure versus control
span.quote: Each batch ( n = 20) consisted of two groups, that is, the experimental group ( n = 10) and the control group ( n = 10).

span.label: escape latency in the water maze
span.term: escape latency in the water maze
span.quote: The relationships between the latencies and the training days of the mice from the experimental and control groups in different batches are shown in Figure 1 .

span.label: percentage of time in the target quadrant
span.term: percentage of time in the target quadrant
span.quote: The percentages of time spent in a target quadrant for the mice from the experimental and control groups in different batches are shown in Figure 3 .

span.label: hippocampal glutamate and GABA concentration
span.quote: The hippocampal amino acid neurotransmitters of the mice from the experimental and control groups in different batches are shown in Figure 4 .

span.label: housing temperature, humidity and light cycle
span.term: housing temperature, humidity and light cycle
span.quote: Five mice were housed in one cage and were kept in a room with constant temperature (22 ± 2°C), humidity (50–60%), and a 12 h/12 h light/dark cycle (lights on at 08:00, lights off at 20:00).

span.label: 70 ± 1.5 dB(A) — day-night equivalent sound pressure level of the combined traffic noise played to the experimental group
span.quote: The L dn , noise exposure intensity for the experimental group was 70 ± 1.5 dB(A)

span.label: 35 dB(A) — background noise level, i.e. the exposure of the control group
span.quote: The L Aeq of the background noise was not more than 35 dB(A), which was the intensity presented to the control group.

span.label: 80 — total number of male ICR mice used, split into four batches
span.quote: A total of 80 healthy male ICR mice (28 days old, weighing 14.4 ± 1.1 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Centre of Zhejiang Province (Hangzhou, China), and were randomly divided into four batches.

span.label: n = 20 (n = 10 and n = 10) — mice per batch, split evenly into experimental and control groups
span.quote: Each batch ( n = 20) consisted of two groups, that is, the experimental group ( n = 10) and the control group ( n = 10).

span.label: 42 days — duration of continuous noise exposure for the experimental group after a 7-day adaptation
span.quote: After an adaptation for 7 days in the laboratory, the mice of the experimental group were continuously exposed to the CTN for 42 days, while for the control group, this was not done.

span.label: 5 and 15 μmol/g — normal hippocampal glutamate range against which the measured values were judged non-toxic
span.quote: The level of Glu was between 5 and 15 μmol/g in the hippocampus of normal mice.

span.label: 2092 pcu/h — highway traffic flux used to reconstruct the combined traffic noise stimulus
span.quote: The two single traffic noises collected were rationally arranged and superimposed to get CTN according to the 24-h traffic flux of highway (2092 pcu/h) and high-speed railway (24 vehicles per hour in the daytime and 12 vehicles per hour at night).

span.label: 90 s — maximum trial duration in the Morris water maze hidden platform test
span.quote: The duration for the trial was 90 s.

span.label: 70 dB(A) — the single exposure level, which produces opposite effects at different durations
span.quote: The Institute of Cancer Research (ICR) mice were exposed to CTN from highways and high-speed railways for 42 days, whose day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L dn ) was 70 dB(A).

span.label: 80 healthy male ICR mice — the whole sample, in four batches of twenty
span.quote: A total of 80 healthy male ICR mice (28 days old, weighing 14.4 ± 1.1 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Centre of Zhejiang Province (Hangzhou, China), and were randomly divided into four batches.

span.label: 42 days — total exposure period across which the four batches were tested
span.quote: The Institute of Cancer Research (ICR) mice were exposed to CTN from highways and high-speed railways for 42 days, whose day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L dn ) was 70 dB(A).

span.label: 71 dB(A) — the level at which an earlier human study found IMPROVED episodic memory - one decibel above this study's exposure
span.quote: However, Stansfeld et al .[ 10 ] found that the road traffic noise whose highest equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L Aeq ) was 71 dB(A) could improve the ability of episodic memory in children.

span.label: 63.5 dB — the level above which combined road-rail noise becomes more annoying than a single dominant source
span.quote: In addition, they found that when the day–night equivalent continuous A-weighted sound pressure level ( L dn ) was greater than 63.5 dB, the percentage of highly annoyed individuals due to the road–rail CTN (the difference in L dn between the two sources was less than or equal to 5 dB) was significantly higher than that due to the one dominant noise (the difference in L dn between the two sources was larger than 5 dB, and the larger one was the dominant noise) with the same L dn .

span.label: 2092 pcu/h — the highway traffic flux used to reconstruct the combined exposure
span.quote: The two single traffic noises collected were rationally arranged and superimposed to get CTN according to the 24-h traffic flux of highway (2092 pcu/h) and high-speed railway (24 vehicles per hour in the daytime and 12 vehicles per hour at night).
